Do you enjoy getting into political discussions online? Are you a masochist, or perhaps autistic? Then Wikipedia is the place for you!

Do you have way too much spare time? Are you a kid, or perhaps a virgin? Then Wikipedia is the place for you also!

None of the above but you care about politics in the age of information? Well then maybe Wikipedia can be the place for you on a boring Sunday afternoon!

Wikipedia has a strong liberal bias, just compare articles such as Fox News and CNN, or Breitbart and Buzzfeed, or any other pairing of your choice - the results might impress you. But not all is loss! The tide might be (very slowly) turning. Would you like to help? Keep in mind that Wikipedia is the 5th most visited website in the world - Trump's article has received 12,300,000+ views during election week!

Anyone may be able to edit Wikipedia, but there are editors watching every page ready to revert any edits you make that might remove their political bias from their pet articles... but! There are rules to the game. Wikipedia is nothing but a democratic bureaucracy. If you follow the rules, you just might be able to improve an article getting rid of its liberal bias - after all, it's far easier to remove than to add content to Wikipedia (more on that later). There are talk pages where editors argue over content added to a page following or not Wikipedia's rules, and whoever makes the best argument - ending the discussion without further opposition from other editors, convincing a large majority of editor or, if the matter at hand is too disputed, ultimately by winning a vote from the community - gets the say on what goes and what doesn't go into an article.

So, are you interested? Meh... a bit maybe? You don't have to engage on politics right away, just create an account! If you see a typo while searching for the average penis size in your country fix it, every positive edit counts to your reputation on the encyclopedia and after a certain amount of edits and account age you get some privileges. When you feel like editing an article on politics come back to this thread and read some of the tips below.

Now for you autistic kids eager to get down to editing controversial articles, here are a few tips:

  • Content must be sourced and sources must be reliable (sorry, neither Breitbart nor Buzzfeed count)

  • See a bunch of low quality sources? Remove it and link to this!

  • Someone added liberal bs to an article? Remove it. They should prove it first.

  • Someone keeps removing your material? You may be able to report them - also follow this rule yourslef. See also: 1RR, ARB.

  • Someone is shitting on an article about a living person? Heh, that's an easy one

  • You raised an issue about something you removed on the talk page and people can't decide on including it back or not? Make it a vote! (ask ask fellow voaters to help you, though that's against the rules so do it off-wiki ;)
